title: Mirror against Crush, on the phrase
listen: The phrase the owner heard Mirror on. Where two notes overlap, Mirror's rectifier makes their sums and differences - partials of neither note - which is what Crush's steps sound like; on the one note held at the end it goes clean again. Crush is rough on every note, alone or not.

title: Mirror on one note, and on a chord
listen: A3 with its major third, held three seconds: nothing, Mirror Both, and Crush 3 bits. On one note Mirror is an octave up and clean (the phrase's last note, above); on a chord it makes the two notes' sums and differences, and that is the crusher the owner heard.

title: Radial Fold, either side of where it starts
listen: A chord on the base sine with Radial on Fold. At a radius of 90 the figure never reaches the circle, and it is Radial off to the bit. At 75 it has just reached it; by 50 the chord is as crushed as Mirror makes it, and 20 is no worse. A small part of the knob does everything.

title: The same on the Slow pad, a quieter sound
listen: The pad is drawn smaller, so its threshold is lower: at 60 Fold does nothing, at 30 it is starting, at 12 it is crushed. Where the knob starts to act depends on how loud the sound is, not on the knob.

title: Radial Clip at its gentlest, on a chord
listen: Clip at a radius of 100 is the setting that ought to be nearly off. On a chord at the base's level it is not: the tanh rounds the summed figure and a little of the chord's products comes through (-27 dB against -60).
